- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices during strong negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.50) — add 3–5% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes — cap forecast at 1–2% below the immediate prior peak.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3 consecutive forecast days exceed true outcome by >2%, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- Lagged overreaction: if forecast is 2–3 days ahead of true price trend, reduce forecast by 1–2% per lag day.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs: if last 3 true values are rising, don’t forecast further increase unless sentiment confirms.
- Use sentiment as momentum filter: if sentiment > 0.20, reduce forecast volatility; if sentiment < -0.30, increase forecast volatility.
